title: The cuff
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: Winter. Alone. Faster. The coat's cuff frays on the mat cutter's edge and Wood watches it happen over four panels and doesn't stop it. A thread, then two. It's the cuff the strip will draw for eleven years. It starts here. The strip is drawn faster than the fraying.

panels.composition: The chore coat's right cuff against the mat cutter's steel edge. A thread catching.

image.prompt: close on a canvas coat cuff catching on the steel edge of a mat cutter, a single thread pulling, black and white, no words

panels.composition: Two threads. The cuff's edge going soft.

image.prompt: close on a canvas cuff with two threads pulled loose, black and white, no words

panels.composition: WOOD's hand, cutting on. Not stopping. The cuff fraying while the corner comes clean.

image.prompt: close on a young man's hand cutting a clean mat corner while his coat cuff frays against the cutter, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The cut done. The cuff frayed. Wood looking at it. Leaving it. The line of the strip faster than the fraying: the whole thing in eighty strokes.

image.prompt: a young man at a mat cutter looking at his frayed coat cuff and leaving it, drawn in a fast sparse line, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen over rough blue pencil; xerox grain; stark spotting; rain in frantic vertical hatching (Arc 1's aesthetic)

notes: The frayed cuff, from the cutter. Eleven years of it start here. Eighty strokes.
